title: A deletion filter in Pyomo

blocks.text: A staffing team's models are LPs and small MILPs, and when one comes back infeasible they want the rows to blame without a commercial solver. HiGHS can tell them whether a model is feasible; the **deletion filter** turns that yes/no answer into an irreducible infeasible subsystem.
Write `deletion_filter(model)` in `iis.py`. It receives an infeasible Pyomo model and returns the sorted names of the rows of one irreducible infeasible subsystem; variable bounds always stay.

items: Deactivate the objective: only feasibility matters. Objectives and constraints both have `.deactivate()` and `.activate()`; for the objective the reference calls `objective.deactivate()` on each one `model.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True)` yields.

Take each active row in turn (`model.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True)`). Call `row.deactivate()` and ask `feasible(model)` (in the starter). If the model is now feasible, the row is part of the conflict: `row.activate()` and keep it. If the model is still infeasible, leave the row out for good.
The rows left active at the end are the subsystem.

blocks.text: The tests use models with one conflict and with two unrelated ones. About ten lines.

from __future__ import annotations

import pyomo.environ as pyo
from pyomo.contrib.solver.common.factory import SolverFactory
from pyomo.contrib.solver.common.results import TerminationCondition


def feasible(model: pyo.ConcreteModel) -> bool:
    """Whether the model's active rows and the variables' bounds have a common point."""
    results = SolverFactory("highs").solve(model, raise_exception_on_nonoptimal_result=False,
                                           load_solutions=False)
    return results.termination_condition != TerminationCondition.provenInfeasible


def deletion_filter(model: pyo.ConcreteModel) -> list[str]:
    """Names of the rows of one irreducible infeasible subsystem of an infeasible model (bounds kept)."""
    for objective in model.component_data_objects(pyo.Objective, active=True):
        objective.deactivate()                     # feasibility is the only question
    rows = list(model.component_data_objects(pyo.Constraint, active=True))
    keep = []
    for row in rows:
        row.deactivate()
        if feasible(model):                        # without this row the rest is feasible: it is needed
            row.activate()
            keep.append(row.name)
    return sorted(keep)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    m.x = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 10))
    m.y = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 10))
    m.a = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x + m.y >= 12)
    m.b = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x <= 3)
    m.c = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.y <= 4)
    m.d = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.x - m.y <= 5)
    print(deletion_filter(m))

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

# Pyomo logs every set it builds and the whole solver log; keep its own logger to warnings.
logging.getLogger("pyomo").setLevel(logging.WARNING)

import pyomo.environ as pyo

from iis import deletion_filter


def shifts(wage_cap, late_cap):
    """Drivers on early and late shifts."""
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    m.early = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 6))
    m.late = pyo.Var(bounds=(0, 6))
    m.need = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.early + m.late >= 11)
    m.late_cap = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.late <= late_cap)
    m.wages = pyo.Constraint(expr=2 * m.early + 3 * m.late <= wage_cap)
    m.balance = pyo.Constraint(expr=m.late - m.early <= 2)
    m.cost = pyo.Objective(expr=2 * m.early + 3 * m.late)
    return m


print("rows kept, wages <= 40, late <= 3:", deletion_filter(shifts(40, 3)))
print("rows kept, wages <= 20, late <= 6:", deletion_filter(shifts(20, 6)))

cases.says: a staffing model whose cover row conflicts with the union cap returns those two rows
a conflict of three rows, any two of which can hold together, returns all three
a model with two unrelated conflicts returns the rows of one of them, not an empty list
